author: EmuCore - Hub
title: One settings model, many surfaces: EmuCoreV's customization system
summary: Background media, cover density, typography, drawer treatment, touch visuals, and game-menu layouts all travel through one observable settings model. The result is broad personalization without each screen inventing its own preference format.
heroAlt: Official gold EmuCoreV Pro emblem used by the customization and branding system

blocks.text: `CustomizationSettings` gathers background path and media type, library-cover scale, application font, custom-font path, text scale, touch-control style, touch press effect, game-menu layout, and drawer style into one immutable value. `CustomizationPreferences` persists that value and exposes a `StateFlow`, allowing the application theme and individual surfaces to observe the same snapshot. The enums are intentionally descriptive—System, Rubik, Exo 2, or Custom fonts; Sidebar, Dashboard, Command Center, or Compact menus; Classic, Compact, Glass, or Console drawers—rather than unrelated numeric switches in each screen.
Imported media is copied into application-owned storage

A selected background or custom font begins as an Android content URI, which may be temporary or controlled by another provider. The preferences layer copies the chosen file into its own managed directory and records the resulting path. Image and video backgrounds are distinguished by MIME type; `CustomizationBackground` can display the appropriate medium behind screen content, apply a scrim, and preserve normal Compose layout above it. Clearing the setting removes the managed copy instead of leaving orphaned personal media.
Typography scales as a system, not as isolated labels

`rememberCustomizedTypography()` maps Rubik and Exo 2 to bundled variable-font resources, can load a custom typeface from the managed path, and falls back safely when a file is invalid. It then applies the selected scale to every Material typography role, including matching line height. Display, headline, title, body, and label styles therefore change coherently. The font license texts for both bundled families are shipped in application assets alongside the font binaries.
Library density is calculated from width and the chosen cover size

Cover scale is constrained between 70 and 150 percent. `LibraryGridSizing.columnsForWidth()` turns that preference and the available width into a bounded column count, while `LibraryScreen` and the customization preview call the same sizing logic. A tablet can gain columns instead of merely stretching phone cards; a larger chosen cover can reduce the count without exceeding the viewport. Home and Library read the active customization through `LocalCustomizationSettings`, so preview and real content share the underlying parameters.
Presets compose values but do not create a second state system

The July 29 sequence began with the core preferences and settings tab, then hardened the live preview and Pro branding in `4edb282f`, and added interface presets and feedback in `0302ae9d`. A preset is useful because it selects a coherent combination, yet the resulting values still land in `CustomizationPreferences`; users can continue editing individual parts afterward. Theme mode remains coordinated with `Theme.kt`, where System, Light, Dark, and Pro select color behavior while customized typography and backgrounds are provided around the same Compose tree.

items: The theme layer owns colors and typography.
CustomizationBackground owns the optional image or video backdrop and scrim.
LibraryGridSizing converts cover scale and width into card columns.
Navigation and emulation surfaces read drawer, menu, and control presentation from the shared settings snapshot.

blocks.text: The gold Pro emblem is a real branding asset introduced with preview-stability work. It is not used as a substitute for settings state: entitlement, theme selection, and visual resources remain separate contracts tested by dedicated branding and customization checks.
